resources.string: Texts, picture messages and chats on this phone
Put a backup from this app or the Chrome extension back on this phone. You see what’s in it first.
A copy of everything in a file of its own, to keep or share.
Message Archivist becomes your SMS app while it restores

Android only lets the SMS app add messages. At the end you switch back to Google Messages. Texts that arrive meanwhile are kept, and Google Messages fetches picture messages afterwards. Nothing already on this phone is added twice.

For group chats: a message you received in a group lists everyone it went to, you included, and this phone doesn’t say its own number. Leave it empty to go ahead without it (group messages you received would show as separate chats).
All of it goes into one file. Next you choose where: on this phone, or Google Drive so it’s safe if the phone isn’t.
The file is bigger, but it’s a complete copy.

Texts, picture messages and group chats, with their exact times. Chat (RCS) messages are in it as Google Messages keeps them on the phone; at the moment it doesn’t keep some you send, so those can be missing.
There are no texts on this phone to back up.
Message Archivist can’t read your texts
To back them up it needs the SMS permission. Allow it in the app’s settings, then try again.

In the Message Archivist extension for Chrome, Settings → Tools → Bring in files… adds it to your archive. From then on the extension keeps it up to date from Google Messages for Web, with the chat messages a phone doesn’t keep.
Pick a backup made before: only what’s new is added, such as today’s messages, or its photos if it was made without them.

Back up to another file from now on: a new one, backed up now, or one you have, brought up to date now.
Android picks the exact time, when the battery isn’t low, and may wait longer to save battery, more so if the app hasn’t been opened for a while.
The file is online, so the whole file is uploaded each time: this often, with photos, can use a lot of data.

Every contact’s numbers, email addresses, work, birthday, labels and relations go into each backup, not only those you’ve texted, so your archive can tie chats from WhatsApp, Telegram and other apps to the right person. Never addresses or notes. Turn off to take them out at the next backup.
“123456 is your verification code”: one-time codes for signing in.
“Reply STOP to opt out”, and links from numbers you don’t know.
Alerts, deliveries and reminders from short codes and business names.

Groups, starred contacts and chats you’ve talked in are always kept. A backup made before drops these chats the next time it’s brought up to date. The Message Archivist extension has the same choices for your archive.
Keep a copy on this phone
Each backup adds to this copy and uploads it, so the file online isn’t downloaded first. Uses %1$s on this phone; turn it off to free that.
Made at the next backup. Each backup then adds to it and uploads it, instead of downloading the file online first.
Not kept: this phone is short of space, so each backup downloads the file online first.
Each backup downloads the whole file online first, then deletes that copy.
Upload less: a small updates file
This backup is online, so every run uploads the whole file. With a small updates file beside it, runs upload only what’s new, and the big file catches up only when that’s worth it.
New messages go into “%1$s”; “%2$s” catches up now and then. To restore or bring it into the extension, use the big file, then this one.

It only puts backups back on this phone. To send texts, make Google Messages your SMS app again.
What you share or add here goes into your next backup, by itself or by hand, and into your archive when you bring that backup in on your computer.
In WhatsApp, open a chat, then ⋮ → More → Export chat, and pick Message Archivist. Include media to keep its photos.

In Facebook: Accounts Center → Download your information, with Messages and the JSON format. When it’s ready, share the .zip to Message Archivist, or add it here. Encrypted chats need Messenger’s own download, on a computer.
In Instagram: Accounts Center → Download your information, with Messages and the JSON format. When it’s ready, share the .zip to Message Archivist, or add it here.
In Snapchat: Settings → My Data, with your chats and Chat Media. When the email comes, share the .zip to Message Archivist, or add it here.
In TikTok: Settings and privacy → Account → Download your data, as JSON. When it’s ready, share the .zip to Message Archivist, or add it here.
In Discord: User Settings → Data & Privacy → Request all of my data. When the email comes, share package.zip to Message Archivist, or add it here. It has only the messages you sent.
Adding it to your phone backup…
%1$s (%2$s) goes into your next backup, and into your archive with it.
There’s nothing to add: share the export file itself (a .zip or .txt), not text.
